$comment: U57 -- the four CAN termination resistors go from a 100 mW 0603 to a 500 mW
0805, and /CAN2_TX's dogleg drops to the Bottom layer to make room for one
of them. Review item 17.
THE FAULT. CANH shorted to +12 V is the canonical automotive CAN failure --
a chafed harness does it. With the H1/H3 jumper fitted that drives the
R10+R14 (and R15+R24) series pair, 120.8 ohm, from 12 V down to whatever the
transceiver holds CANL at. At CANL ~1.5-2.5 V that is 78-87 mA, so 0.37-0.46 W
PER RESISTOR. Against a 0603's 100 mW that is 3.7-4.6x.
Not a functional defect today: thick-film parts fail OPEN, so the bus loses
termination and keeps working, and the TJA1051 survives bus shorts by
ISO 11898-2. It is hardening -- but the board is going in a car, so it is
hardening worth having.
THE PART. C3959530, Panasonic ERJP06F60R4V, 0805, 60.4 ohm +/-1%, 500 mW,
400 V, anti-surge. 500 mW covers the 0.37-0.46 W single-fault case at
1.1-1.35x. It does NOT cover the 0.60 W double fault (CANH to 12 V AND CANL
hard-grounded simultaneously) -- that needs the 1206 ERJ-P08, and see below
for why the 1206 was rejected. 13,988 in stock.
A STANDARD 0805 DOES NOT FIX THIS. The common 0805 is 125 mW, which is still
3-3.7x over; the ordinary uprated one is 250 mW, still 1.5-1.8x over. Only
the anti-surge ERJ-P06 clears it, so this is a specific part, not a size.
WHY NOT THE 1206 (660 mW). It was tried first and measured: it does not fit.
R10 overlapped R14 and R24 overlapped P2, and the fix cascades -- R15 cannot
be a vertical 1206 at all (it needs 5.116 mm between /CAN2_RX at y=127.333
and /CAN2_TX at y=131.579, and there are 4.246 mm), so it has to rotate and
move 2.5 mm east, which drags /CAN2_TERM across /CAN2_TX. Every arrangement
ended in a three-net re-layout of the corner to buy the double-fault margin
on a fault that already needs two simultaneous harness shorts. The 0805
buys the single-fault margin for two vias.
R10 AND R14 DO NOT MOVE AT ALL, and neither do their tracks. The 0603 pad
centres sit at +/-0.7535 from the body centre; the 0805 pad spans 0.4337 to
1.5663 from it, so every existing stub still lands well inside the new pad
(0.32 mm from the nearest edge). Measured clearance after the swap: R10
+0.527 mm to /+3V3, R14 +0.247 mm to /CAN1_TERM, both against a 0.1016 mm
rule.
R15 MOVES 0.70 mm NORTH. As a vertical 0805 at y=130.000 its lower pad
overlaps the /CAN2_TX run at y=131.579 by 0.114 mm. The usable band is
127.460 (RX edge) to 131.452 (TX edge) = 3.992 mm against the 3.336 mm an
0805 needs with clearance, so it fits -- just not centred where it was.
At y=129.300 it clears TX by 0.586 mm and RX by 0.274 mm.
R24 IS THE ONE THAT NEEDED THE ROUTING CHANGE, and it is worth recording why,
because it is not a clearance problem that moving the part can solve. R24 is
pinned: /CAN2_L has to run west at y=130 to P2.2, so R24 must sit west of
where /CAN2_TX steps down, and P2's courtyard stops it going further west. A
2D sweep of 168 positions found NO legal spot -- /CAN2_TX boxes the pocket on
three sides at once (the y=131.579 run below, the y=128.531 run above, and
the dogleg between them). The best position on the board was +0.051 mm,
against a 0.1016 mm rule.
And the dogleg cannot simply move: west of x~132 /CAN2_TX must stay above
/CAN2_L (y=130) and below /CAN2_RX (y=127.333), and east of x~134 it is at
y=131.579, so the step is forced into exactly the pocket R24 occupies.
SO THE DOGLEG GOES TO THE BOTTOM LAYER -- the three Top segments between
(133.946,131.579) and (131.914,128.531) are re-laid identically on Bottom
with a via at each end. The Top run either side is untouched. Bottom in this
pocket (x 128..137, y 126..133) is completely empty apart from one /CAN2_RX
via 2.21 mm away, and /CAN2_RX already layer-hops through this same corner
on Inner2, so this is the established pattern here rather than a new one.
With the dogleg gone from Top, R24 stays exactly where it is.
The two vias drill 0.25, not the tool default of 0.30: 233 of the board's
236 vias are 0.6/0.25 and adding a third drill size buys nothing. The one
0.5/0.20 outlier (BTN1 at U1.93) is what sets the declared minimum hole
size in fab/ORDER.md, and that is unchanged by this edit.
R10'S DESIGNATOR MOVES TO THE OTHER SIDE. Swapping a land pattern re-seats
the reference field at the new library's offset -- 1.917 mm from centre
instead of 1.537 -- and that 0.38 mm put 'R10' straight onto R14's silk
(four silk_overlap warnings, one touching at 0.000 mm). The text is rotated
with the part, so it is 1.696 x 3.155 mm and taller than R10's own body:
above and below are blocked by the part it labels, and only the two sides
are viable. It goes west to x=161.000, clear by 0.659 mm against a 0.150 mm
rule, and still unambiguously nearer R10 than any other part.
Both footprints arrived from JLCImport with NO courtyard -- all 148 parts on
this board have one -- so a courtyard was authored at 0.25 mm over the pads
(and enclosing the silk) before any of the above was measured.
No net changes, so no KTD12 GUI sync. The schematic's Footprint and supplier
fields are updated in the same commit, because --schematic-parity is the only
check that compares a footprint to its symbol.

steps.step: 1/3  swap all four to the 500 mW anti-surge 0805; only R15 moves
2/3  lift /CAN2_TX's dogleg off Top, and free R15's TERM stub
3/3  re-lay the dogleg on Bottom, and re-land R15's TERM stub
